provenance.serialisation: manifest rows sorted by path; each row serialised UTF-8 as "path\0size\0sha256" when the file is present and "path\0absent\0absent" when it is declared but absent; rows joined by \n with a trailing \n; digest = sha256 of that blob. Declared files that are absent are serialised explicitly, never skipped.
provenance.rule: sha256 over the canonical file manifest of the published source tree: paths matching ['pyproject.toml', 'uv.lock', 'src/windcheck/*.py', 'engines/*.cpp', 'engines/*.h', 'bench/*.py'] relative to the repository root, excluding __pycache__, serialised by the frozen rule below. Recompute with `uv run python -m windcheck.provenance`; no repository history is required.

superseded_digests.reason: v0.1.0-beta as first published. Its emitted point collections lacked the vc_pointcollections_json_version envelope that volume-cartographer's PointCollections loader requires, so they could not be opened in VC3D. Geometry, censuses, meshes and hashes are unaffected.

v0.1.0-beta after the point-collection envelope fix. Superseded by the disclosure of the upstream z <= 0 validity rule in every check certificate, and by writers that recompute meta.json bbox from the points they emit instead of copying the source. No census, mesh, hash or retention figure changes.

superseded by the publication of the 84,316-patch audit: three new bench drivers (patch_audit, patch_diagnose, patch_baseline_tiles). No census, mesh, hash or retention figure in the pinned corpus changes.
superseded by the pair-composition test (bench/patch_pairs.py). No census, mesh, hash or retention figure in the pinned corpus changes.
superseded by the full-corpus expansion and the disagreement study. The released transverse-clean outputs and every retention figure are unchanged.

superseded by the publication of check-pairs: the pairwise merge-edge conflict test (src/windcheck/pairs.py), the multi-surface census engine it runs on, and the 459-pair reproducible example in results/pairs/. The released transverse-clean outputs and every retention figure are unchanged.

superseded by the expansion-corpus release: bench/expand_bases.py and bench/build_expansion_index.py added, bench/excise_shadow.py extended to resolve segments entirely from a base manifest (voxel scale may be null; physical-unit fields follow it). Pinned-corpus certificates and meshes are unaffected.

superseded by the topology-transaction release: src/windcheck/transaction.py (staged atomic transaction CLI), the case-study analysis drivers (bench/fiesta_adapter.py, bench/fiesta_gate.py, bench/cover_applicability.py) and the cover-applicability negative. Prior certificates unaffected.

superseded by the transaction hotfix: the authoritative transaction report is committed inside the output before promotion and --report becomes a post-commit copy; the official validator resolves through PATH once and the resolved binary is invoked and hashed; a transform report claiming handover no longer outranks a nonzero adapter exit. No census, mesh, hash or retention figure changes.

mesh_identity_rule: mesh identity is a content manifest over every file a tifxyz reader consumes semantically -- x/y/z.tif, mask.tif or mask.png, meta.json -- not the coordinate planes alone, so a mask change (the carrier of an excision) cannot leave a recorded mesh hash valid.
base_kind_rule: base_kind is decided by SEMANTIC MANIFEST EQUALITY -- the input mesh's content manifest against the original published mesh's -- and never by path, because paths change in downloaded archives and fresh working directories. Index generation fails loudly when a certificate's declared base_kind disagrees with that hash-verified answer.
terminology: Every retention figure on this page is represented surface retained: canonical quad area that survives the cut, divided by the canonical quad area of the stated denominator. It is a geometric measure of the mesh, and nothing more.

definitions.represented_surface_retained: Every retention figure on this page is represented surface retained: canonical quad area that survives the cut, divided by the canonical quad area of the stated denominator. It is a geometric measure of the mesh, and nothing more.
definitions.operational_denominator: measured against the PRE-EXCISION BASE, i.e. the mesh that was actually cut. Where that base is a displacement-repaired mesh rather than the published original, this denominator measures what the excision cost relative to the surface it was handed.
definitions.headline_denominator: measured against the ORIGINAL PUBLISHED mesh: the removed ORIGINAL quad indices are priced using the ORIGINAL published coordinates, and divided by the canonical area of the original mesh's retained quads. When the base IS the original mesh the two denominators coincide by construction.
definitions.R_main: R_main(C) = area(largest output descendant of input component C) / area(C), reported per INPUT component. It detects a cut that scores near-100% on area while shattering a component into pieces.
definitions.core_gate: The 99.9%-AREA CORE is the smallest prefix of the input components, sorted by canonical area, whose cumulative area reaches 99.9% of the input retained area. The core gate passes when every component in that core has R_main >= 0.90.

denominators.operational: measured against the PRE-EXCISION BASE, i.e. the mesh that was actually cut. Where that base is a displacement-repaired mesh rather than the published original, this denominator measures what the excision cost relative to the surface it was handed.
denominators.headline: measured against the ORIGINAL PUBLISHED mesh: the removed ORIGINAL quad indices are priced using the ORIGINAL published coordinates, and divided by the canonical area of the original mesh's retained quads. When the base IS the original mesh the two denominators coincide by construction.

retention.headline_population_note: The headline denominator is evaluated over all 185 pinned artifacts: 179 carry a priced original-coordinate area, and 6 are triangle-empty or invalid inputs that carry no area at all and so enter with zero on both sides of the ratio. Segments that were never cut are priced at exactly 1.0 against the full canonical area of their original published mesh, recovered through bench/headline_decision.py so that both artifacts report the same figure over the same population.

denominator_divergence.note: Difference between the two per-segment retention fractions. It is exactly zero wherever the base IS the original published mesh, and it is what the displacement repair costs elsewhere.

retention.coverage_note: Segments that were already clean carry no priced-area block, because nothing was cut. Under the operational denominator the certificate still records the area of the base that was handed to the cut, so they price themselves. Under the headline denominator the original-coordinate area is on the certificate only where the base IS the original published mesh; where the base was displacement-repaired it is recovered by re-reading the original mesh, memoised in out/headline_original_areas.json. Either way the segment enters the headline denominator with a retained fraction of exactly 1.0 rather than being dropped.

fragmentation.core_gate_definition: The 99.9%-AREA CORE is the smallest prefix of the input components, sorted by canonical area, whose cumulative area reaches 99.9% of the input retained area. The core gate passes when every component in that core has R_main >= 0.90.
fragmentation.R_main_definition: R_main(C) = area(largest output descendant of input component C) / area(C), reported per INPUT component. It detects a cut that scores near-100% on area while shattering a component into pieces.

archive.proposed_split_rationale: One archive per scroll. The five scrolls are independently useful, the split keeps every archive under 1 GiB, and each archive is self-describing because it carries a copy of the shared manifests. No archive is created by this script.
